description: Download a Eurostat dataset through the SDMX bulk TSV endpoint and stage it as a SQL table on the dataframe canvas — the route to a whole dataset, where eurostat_query_dataset is the route to a slice. It is expanded into one row per non-blank TSV cell; absentCellCount says which rows are not observations. Filter keys come from eurostat_get_dataset_info and values from eurostat_get_dimension_values. Two budgets bound every transfer: a decoded-byte budget (50 MiB by default) and a time budget counted from the start of the call (55 seconds by default, inside the 60 seconds an MCP client waits), so a download that reaches the time budget returns after about 55 seconds. Reached after rows have streamed, either budget keeps them as a prefix with budgetExceeded set; reached before the first row, the call fails. Only preview_limit rows come back inline; without a canvas the rest are not kept.

canvas_id.description: A canvasId from an earlier staging response, to stage this download beside its tables for joins; omit for a fresh canvas.

dataset_code.description: Dataset code (e.g., "nama_10_gdp"). Filter a DS-* code (Comext trade or PRODCOM, in any case): an unfiltered download of a large collection is refused as extraction_too_big, and its trade flows mix annual and monthly series, so filter freq.

filters.description: Map of dimension code → values to keep, e.g. {"unit": ["CP_MEUR"], "geo": ["DE", "FR"]}. Keys match in any case; a key the dataset lacks, "time" included (use since_period/until_period), is rejected with its dimension list. An empty array or a blank value is no filter. A value holding "+" is split into separate values (OR). A value holding "." is rejected as invalid_dimension before any request: no Eurostat code contains one. A value Eurostat does not know fails the download as invalid_dimension; a valid one with no observation in the selected periods is named in emptyValues.

preview_limit.description: Rows echoed inline, from the start of the download. Default 25; positive integers above 500 are clamped to 500 with a notice. The staged table, when there is one, holds every row.

since_period.description: Start of the range, inclusive: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-Qn (1–4), YYYY-Sn (1–2), YYYY-Tn (1–3), YYYY-Mnn (01–12), YYYY-Wnn (up to 53) or YYYY-Dnnn (up to 366), e.g. "2020", "2023-Q1", "2024-01". A range is the most effective way to shrink a download. Any form works on any dataset, but Eurostat keeps only periods wholly inside the range, per frequency: a bound that falls inside a period excludes it, and a notice names that period when the TSV header shows its frequency. A one-day range (both bounds on the same day) selects that day alone. A malformed or non-existent period, or a since_period after until_period, fails as invalid_period.

until_period.description: End of the range, inclusive (e.g., "2024"), in the forms and under the wholly-inside rule of since_period. Omit for data through the latest period.

name: eurostat_download_dataset

absentCellCount.description: An unflagged ":" row (obs_value null with no flag, status or text) is not an observation: it is a period its series lacks, or a period of a frequency the series has no observation of. This counts the first kind: rows at a period of a frequency the same series carries in another downloaded row, inside that frequency's span from its first to its latest period any downloaded row has an observation in. Rows before or after the span are named in the notice instead, and rows at a frequency the series has no observation of (mixed-frequency padding, or a series that is ":" throughout) are left out. A flagged ":" or a text value is an observation. Part of rowCount and missingCount; a budget-cut download counts over its prefix.

appliedQuery.description: The bulk request as the server built it.

filters.description: Filters sent to Eurostat: "+" values split, blank values and empty dimensions dropped.

url.description: The SDMX request URL, to reproduce the download. A one-day range asks for that day and the next, so the URL ends a day past untilPeriod.

budgetExceeded.description: True when the byte budget or the time budget counted from the start of the call ended the transfer early: the rows are a prefix, and the notice names which budget. Where a time cut lands depends on how fast the body arrived, so a repeat can stop at a different row.

bytesRead.description: Decoded TSV bytes read, never more than the byte budget (50 MiB by default). With budgetExceeded true, a value equal to the byte budget means that budget ended the transfer; a smaller one, that the time budget did.

canvasId.description: Canvas holding the staged table; pass it as canvas_id to the dataframe tools or a later staging call. Omitted when nothing was staged.

compressed.description: True when the body arrived gzip-compressed.

dimensionsUsed.description: Dimension codes of the downloaded rows, in key order, from the TSV header; the period is the "time" column.

emptyValues.description: Valid filter values with no observation in the download, by filter key, as sent; such a value can have data in other periods or beside other filter values. Omitted when every filter value has an observation, and when budgetExceeded is true, since the rows not downloaded could hold any of them.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `byte_budget_exceeded`: The byte budget ran out before a complete header and first row were read. `not_found`: The dataset code is not available for dissemination. `invalid_dimension`: A filter key is not a dimension of this dataset; the error names every such key and lists the dataset's dimensions in key order; a filter value contains "." (rejected before any request); Eurostat rejects a filter value; or the period range selects no period of the dataset, missing its coverage or holding no whole period. `filter_arity`: Eurostat rejected the filter key's number of positions: the dataset's structure changed since it was read. `invalid_period`: A period bound is not an accepted form or names a period that does not exist, or since_period starts after until_period ends (bounds of different frequencies compare by day). Checked before any request. `async_queued`: Eurostat queued the extraction instead of sending data: it prepares it in the background and serves the identical download minutes later. The server sends the request once and does not repeat it. `no_results`: The download yielded no row: a header-only table, or a one-day range whose only cells fall on the next day (see appliedQuery.url). Nothing is staged, and no canvas is created or touched. `extraction_too_big`: Eurostat refused the extraction as too large: past its 5,000,000-row limit, or an unfiltered download of a large DS-* collection, which it serves only filtered. `upstream_fault`: Eurostat's data endpoint, or a filtered download's structure endpoint, failed or was unreachable on every attempt, broke the body off, or sent an unmodeled fault, a non-TSV body or an unusable structure; retryable says whether a later call can succeed. `retry_deadline_exceeded`: The call's time budget (55 seconds by default, counted from the start of the call, every attempt and a filtered download's structure read included) ran out before the first row arrived; reached later, it keeps the rows as a prefix with budgetExceeded instead. Or a filtered download's structure read did not answer within its deadline. `canvas_not_found`: canvas_id is unknown or has expired. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

missingCount.description: Rows with obs_value null: observations published without a number (a flagged ":" or a text value), and every unflagged ":" row (see absentCellCount).

notice.description: Disclosures on every download: the staged table with the eurostat_dataframe_describe then eurostat_dataframe_query sequence, or without a canvas what was kept inline. Before it, when they apply: a period a bound excludes, the budget that stopped the transfer, the unflagged ":" rows (see absentCellCount) before or after a frequency's span, inside it and from mixed frequencies, emptyValues (up to 24 named), and the inline-preview length.

observations.description: The first preview_limit rows of the download, in the order Eurostat streamed them. A prefix of the staged table, not a sample.

items.description: One downloaded row: one column per dimension with its code, "time", then obs_value, obs_flag, obs_flag_label, conf_status, conf_status_label (a label is null when Eurostat publishes none). DS-* rows add obs_value_text: a value published as text, such as a PRODCOM unit ("KG"), with obs_value null; PRODCOM's ":C" arrives as conf_status "C".

periodRange.description: Period coverage of the downloaded observations; narrower than the dataset when budgetExceeded is true or a range was set.

end.description: Latest period of a row carrying an observation. Omitted, with the other bound, when no row carries an observation.

start.description: Earliest period of a row carrying an observation; an unflagged ":" row sets no bound. Omitted, with the other bound, when no row carries an observation.

rowCount.description: Rows downloaded, one per non-blank TSV cell, unflagged ":" rows included (see absentCellCount).

stagedRowCount.description: Rows staged; equals rowCount. Omitted with tableName.

tableName.description: Canvas table holding every downloaded row. Call eurostat_dataframe_describe with canvasId for its columns first, then eurostat_dataframe_query. Omitted without a dataframe canvas, when only the inline rows survive the call.

totalCount.description: Rows downloaded, equal to rowCount (see absentCellCount). observations holds only the first preview_limit; budgetExceeded, not this count, says whether the download is whole.

title: Download Eurostat Dataset
